characters.name: Darrow
characters.description: A sixteen-year-old Red miner on Mars with red hair, skilled as a Helldiver who operates the drill machines. He is defiant, restless, and deeply driven to succeed despite the warnings of his elders.
key_events: Navigates a deep tunnel to mine helium-3
Engages in a heated argument with his uncle and crew about risk and the Laurel
Decides to take a dangerous risk by jumping down to manually scan a potential gas pocket

characters.name: Kieran
characters.description: Darrow's elder brother, characterized by the narrator as someone who values caution and is less stoic than expected.
key_events: Advised Darrow to obey their uncle and wait for the scan

characters.name: Leanna
characters.description: Darrow's sister who expresses grief through lament.

characters.name: Eo
characters.description: Darrow's wife, a small, resilient woman with red hair who believes the Laurel is a manipulative tool used by the Society.
key_events: Frequently discussed the injustice of their life with Darrow

characters.name: Narol
characters.description: Darrow's uncle and the headTalk for their mining crew, often drunk and heavily risk-averse.
key_events: Ordered Darrow to stop drilling due to a perceived gas pocket
Urged Darrow to practice patience and obedience

characters.name: Barlow
characters.description: An older, cynical member of the mining crew who mocks Darrow.
key_events: Mocked Darrow's confidence and joked about taking his wife

characters.name: Loran
key_events: Encouraged Darrow to ignore the safety protocols to beat Gamma clan

summary: Darrow is a sixteen-year-old Helldiver living in the underground mining colony of Lykos on Mars. The story is established in a world where the Red clan mines for the Society, governed by a system of strict quotas and rewards like the Laurel—a prize that grants extra rations to the most productive miners. Darrow works deep in the tunnels, operating complex clawDrills in a sweltering, dangerous environment while encased in a protective frysuit. He is driven, reckless, and frustrated by the cautious, slow-moving nature of his elders, including his uncle, Narol, who serves as the crew's headTalk. The memory of his father's execution by the Society looms over him, fueling his quiet resentment toward the status quo. During a shift, Darrow identifies a potential vein of helium-3 but is ordered by Narol to halt operations to check for a gas pocket. Against the advice of his brother Kieran and the warnings from the older crew members, Darrow perceives the delay as cowardly and a waste of their potential to finally win the Laurel away from the dominant Gamma clan. Driven by a desire to provide for his wife, Eo, and a disdain for the passive submission expected of his people, Darrow defies the commands from above. He leaves the safety of his drill holster to perform a manual scan of the gas pocket himself. He descends deep into the tunnel, braving the lethal heat of the drills, determined to secure the win regardless of the personal cost.
